identityTradability.exchangeName: Arm Holdings plc - American Depositary Shares

discovery-weak-signals.name: Platform expansion
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Arm is extending from licensed IP/CSS into production silicon while retaining ecosystem distribution across cloud, edge and physical AI.

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI infrastructure leverage
discovery-weak-signals.basis: AGI CPU and Neoverse CSS N4 directly target CPU-intensive agentic-AI and data-center workloads.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Ecosystem/network effects
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Arm cites broad cloud, OEM, software and physical-AI participation plus a developer ecosystem exceeding 22 million.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Business-model transition risk
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Selling production silicon introduces inventory, supply-chain, customer-channel and execution exposures beyond the historical IP-licensing model.

expectations-execution.name: Execution versus narrative
expectations-execution.basis: Multiple 2026 product and ecosystem milestones show delivery against the strategic expansion announced in March.

expectations-execution.name: Expectation burden
expectations-execution.basis: Broader ambitions increase the proof required on production volume, margins, customer conversion and ecosystem coexistence.

expectations-execution.name: Market expansion
expectations-execution.basis: Cloud agentic AI, edge/mobile AI and physical AI enlarge the addressable workload surface for Arm architecture.

expectations-execution.name: Security-level valuation attractiveness
expectations-execution.basis: No canonical live valuation/entry input is part of this work item; no price-based recommendation is promoted.

thesisQuality.basis: Broad royalty/licensing compute-IP footprint supports structural thesis.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: FY2026 and Q4 show strong double-digit growth and profitability.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current triple-digit earnings multiples imply extreme expectations.

catalystScore.basis: AI/cloud/edge licensing and royalty conversion plus Nov. earnings create catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Current reporting is strong but concentrated control reduces governance independence.

alignment2036.basis: Architecture portfolio directly enables heterogeneous future compute.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Licensing, royalties, CSS and tools reinforce a common architecture ecosystem.

bottleneckControl.basis: Pervasive architecture/IP position creates a major compute-design control point.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Asset-light model and diversified compute end markets support robustness.

substitutionResilience.basis: Installed architecture/software ecosystem creates substantial switching friction.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Asset-light IP model and strong liquidity reduce direct manufacturing exposure.

pricingPower.basis: Near-98% Q4 GAAP gross margin demonstrates exceptional value capture.

riskEvidence.basis: Valuation, control concentration, cyclicality and architecture substitution are material risks.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current primary filings plus independent valuation evidence support reproducible scoring.

scoreRecord.thesis: Arm's pervasive architecture and royalty model form a durable control layer for increasingly heterogeneous AI, cloud, automotive and edge compute.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: The current valuation prices extraordinary execution while concentrated control and RISC-V substitution constrain margin of safety.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: FY2027 Q2 results expected November 4, 2026 and continued AI/cloud CSS royalty conversion.

items.risk: Customer concentration can transmit a few customers' strategic changes directly into Arm economics.
Architecture substitution and customer in-house design choices remain credible long-run pressure points.
Top-five customer concentration is 57% of FY2026 revenue.
SoftBank/affiliate arrangements create related-party dependence requiring conservative interpretation.
Production-silicon expansion can create channel tension with licensees that historically used Arm IP to differentiate their own chips.
AGI CPU success depends on manufacturing, packaging, system integration and customer deployment execution that Arm historically did not own at this scale.
Arm remains exposed to semiconductor export controls, customer concentration and architecture competition from x86 and RISC-V ecosystems.
Named ecosystem participation should not be interpreted as committed production revenue unless contracts, shipments or financial disclosures support it.
Direct silicon increases capital/execution complexity and could pressure economics if volumes do not scale sufficiently.
No canonical live valuation or entry recommendation is asserted; absence of that optional input is non-gating.
Extreme valuation and architecture substitution risk.

contradictions.contradiction: Broad AI-platform narrative coexists with still-material mobile royalty concentration and high customer concentration.
contradictions.resolution: Treat diversification as strengthening but incomplete, not as a present contradiction requiring blockage.

contradictions.claim: Arm's ecosystem breadth is a core advantage, but direct silicon entry can also compete with parts of that same ecosystem.
contradictions.resolution: Treat ecosystem expansion and channel-conflict risk as simultaneous facts; do not net away the conflict without customer-level evidence.

contradictions.claim: Product cadence and ecosystem breadth are strengthening while evidence for production-scale AGI CPU economics remains limited.
contradictions.resolution: Record product/ecosystem execution as positive but keep revenue conversion and margin realization as explicit future evidence rather than assuming them.
